## Analysis at each round
### Round 1
There are no trials in this search yet. In generation 0, all 84 trials across every network and recipe scored exactly 0, and training success was 0 as well. When the result is zero whatever the architecture, the cause is probably shared, not a weak network. One shared cause fits: success needs the agent to choose DONE at exactly the right step. With about 250 legal placements, DONE starts with roughly 0.4% probability per step and gets less likely as placements are rewarded. The +1 exact-build bonus is therefore almost never seen, and the agent never learns to stop. The one DONE-bias trial set the bias to −2, which made DONE even rarer. Because every score so far is 0, we have no estimate of seed noise, so any nonzero result is worth confirming. This round tests the DONE-exploration idea: the bias change on its own, then a DONE path that reads the missing cells directly, then that path with a sample-richer recipe.

### Round 2
All 87 trials so far, across generation 0 and round 1, scored exactly 0 on dev and in training. That includes round 1's DONE priors, its DONE-specific branch and the round 1 recipe with 1.86x as many samples. So DONE exploration alone is not the bottleneck. Because nothing has scored, seed noise is still unknown and no idea can be ranked against another. A competent policy should solve at least some 6-brick designs, so the agent is probably not learning useful placements at all. It might be learning too slowly, or this world's quirk may break an assumption in the shared conv/pool design. The remaining trials should cover settings that have never been tried, rather than repeat ideas that already failed: lr 3e-3 with 1024 environments, gae_lambda 0.8 and 1 epoch; a much smaller network; and a new trunk family (MLP-Mixer token mixing with learned positions), plus a zero-initialised learned remapping from cells to anchors that is robust to the layout.

### Round 3
All 90 trials so far, in generation 0 and this search, score 0 on both training and dev success. That includes the DONE priors, a dedicated DONE path, a 1-epoch run with 1,024 environments at lr 3e-3, a tiny local network, and a mixer with a learned anchor remap. So the agent is failing to learn at all, not failing to generalise, and seed noise still can't be measured. Two areas are still untested. The first is initialisation: no trial has used the standard PPO setup (orthogonal weights, near-zero policy outputs, so the starting policy is nearly uniform over legal actions). With default initialisation, random biases in the starting logits may cause early mistakes that can't be undone, because bricks can't be removed. The second is horizon: gamma has never gone above 0.99 or gae_lambda above 0.95. If this world's reward is sparser than described, the +1 for an exact build needs a long credit horizon. This round tests each change alone, plus one bet combining both with more samples.

### Round 4
All 9 trials in this search scored 0, as did all 84 in generation 0. That includes training success, so the agent is not learning to build at all; the problem is not generalisation. The DONE prior, a dedicated DONE path, orthogonal init, a long credit horizon, maximum throughput, a tiny network and a mixer with a learned remap all failed. No seed noise can be measured. Recipe axes never tried: clip_eps 0.3, very small minibatch counts, and many small updates combined with a large clip. A direct calculation shows that the default recipe gives only about 32 PPO updates. Clipping at 0.2 then limits how far the policy can move away from uniform over roughly 250 actions. As the last round, these are combined bets on many sharp updates, each paired with the init fixes, and each with a different network: the starting net, a normalised deeper trunk, and a shallow footprint-local net. Even if they score 0, they rule out the update-count explanation.
